title: Influencer Detained for Forcing Airport Volunteer to Remove Mask
content: On October 17, Southern Metropolis Daily reported that popular airline reviewer and influencer 'Xiaohu Xing' was exposed for forcing a female volunteer to remove her mask at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport. After being refused, he repeatedly harassed the volunteer and airport staff, and attempted to forcibly remove her mask by hand. He later argued with a male passenger who tried to intervene, seriously disrupting check-in operations. The Shenzhen Airport Police confirmed that the man, Wang, harassed volunteers under the influence of alcohol and was administratively detained. Public opinion suggests that influencers with large followings bear greater social responsibility and must adhere to laws and social norms. Provoking incidents for attention will only lead to consequences.

title: Parents Catch School Cafeteria Serving Spoiled Meat in Kunming
content: On October 17, China National Radio reported that parents at Yunzi Middle School in Guandu District, Kunming, discovered spoiled raw meat in the student cafeteria, raising widespread concern. In the video, a parent emotionally accused the cafeteria of serving rotten meat and stated that the police had been notified. According to the official WeChat account of Guandu District, a preliminary investigation found that the raw pork had an abnormal odor. Authorities sealed the ingredients, launched traceability checks, and began an investigation. The school cafeteria has since ceased operations. Public opinion emphasized that school food safety issues should not be left to parents to uncover, and that systemic reform is needed to address long-standing safety problems masked by superficial records.

title: Domestic 3A Game 'Black Myth: Wukong' Officially Launched
content: Xinhua News Agency reported on August 23 that China's first domestic '3A' game, Black Myth: Wukong, continues to stir up the market. Data shows that the game has sold over 3 million copies on the international gaming platform Steam, and combined with sales from Epic Games, WeGame, and PlayStation platforms, total sales exceed 4.5 million copies, with total revenue surpassing 1.5 billion RMB. This sets a new record for domestic game sales. Public opinion suggests that the game reinterprets Eastern mythology from a modern perspective, reflecting China’s renewed cultural confidence and breaking overseas stereotypes about Chinese culture, presenting a more diverse and modern image of China.

title: China's National Football Team Loses 0-7 to Japan
content: The Paper reported that on September 5, in the opening match of the FIFA 2026 World Cup Asian Qualifiers, China’s national football team faced Japan away and lost 0-7. This defeat set multiple humiliating records: largest loss to Japan, most goals conceded in a World Cup qualifier, and the biggest score gap in China’s qualifier history. Previously, the worst loss was 0-8 in a friendly against Brazil in 2012. Public opinion suggests that the game clearly showed a wide gap in skills, not caused by individual player performance, but by overall weakness. Recognizing this, Chinese football should accept the failure calmly and strive for genuine reform.

title: Post-95 Researcher with 4 PhDs and 2 Postdocs Sparks Skepticism
content: Guangming.com reported that on October 11, the Inner Mongolia Institute of National Culture and Arts released resumes of several researchers, including Zhao Zijian, a post-95 researcher claiming 4 PhDs, 2 postdoctoral fellowships, and 22 part-time social roles. The news drew widespread media and public attention. On October 10, the institute suspended Zhao's employment and began an investigation into his academic credentials. Public opinion argues this isn’t a joke but a symptom of academic chaos, calling for urgent scrutiny into 'watered-down degrees' and fake institutions that threaten academic integrity.

title: Gradual Delay of Legal Retirement Age to Start Next Year
content: According to CCTV News, on the 13th, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress voted to implement a plan for gradually delaying the statutory retirement age. Starting January 1, 2025, China will spend 15 years gradually raising the retirement age: from 60 to 63 for male workers, and from 50 or 55 to 55 or 58 for female workers, depending on occupation. This marks the first adjustment to retirement age since the 1950s. Public attention has turned to how this shift will impact labor dynamics and elderly welfare.

title: Professor at Huazhong Agricultural University Reported for Academic Fraud
content: On January 16, 2024, netizens revealed a report letter signed and fingerprinted by multiple students from Huazhong Agricultural University, accusing their supervisor, Professor Huang Feiruo, of academic misconduct such as data tampering and fabricating experimental results. On February 6, the university confirmed the misconduct, terminated Huang’s contract, and retracted related papers and projects. The whistleblowers, including 11 students, exposed issues of data manipulation and plagiarism. Huang had published over 40 SCI papers since becoming a professor in 2017, but his unethical practices led to severe consequences. The case sparked concern over research ethics and whistleblower protection, underscoring the need for integrity in academia.

title: Vocational Student Ranks 12th Globally in Math Competition
content: Reported on June 13, Jiang Ping, a 17-year-old vocational student from Huaian, Jiangsu, ranked 12th globally in an international math competition, becoming the first secondary school student to reach the finals. Most of the 801 finalists are from prestigious universities such as Tsinghua, Peking, MIT, and Cambridge. Jiang, a fashion design major, self-studied advanced math like PDEs for two years. Her story gained public support but later drew skepticism—netizens questioned her past grades, noticed errors in her blackboard writing, and suspected cheating due to the open-book format. On June 27, reports revealed she scored 83 on a recent math test, fueling accusations of academic dishonesty in the Alibaba-sponsored contest.

title: 'Elderly Car' Drives Wrong Way on Chengya Expressway and Crashes
content: Guangming.com reported on October 14 that a small electric vehicle, known as 'elderly car,' was involved in a fatal accident on the Chengya Expressway in Sichuan. The vehicle illegally entered the expressway via a toll gate and drove against traffic in the overtaking lane, resulting in a collision that killed two occupants. Toll station staff attempted to stop the vehicle but failed. Public opinion emphasizes the need for stricter measures to prevent such unregulated vehicles from accessing highways, and that toll gates must serve as effective enforcement points.

title: Nearly 1,500 New Students at Guangdong University Forfeit Admission
content: On October 21, Upstream News reported that Guangdong Baiyun University publicized a list of 1,477 newly admitted students for the 2024 class who are considered to have forfeited their admission. These students either failed to report on time, did not complete leave procedures, or did not retain their admission status. The university responded that these students may have chosen to retake the college entrance exam. The news sparked heated discussion online.

title: Yao Ming Resigns as Chairman of the Chinese Basketball Association
content: According to CCTV News, on October 31, the 10th Executive Committee Meeting of the Chinese Basketball Association was held in Beijing. The committee accepted Yao Ming's resignation as chairman and elected Guo Zhenming as his successor. In a media interview, Yao expressed that his passion for basketball remains unchanged. He emphasized that the development of Chinese basketball involves various aspects such as international exchanges, youth training, public welfare, industry research, and culture. Yao stated that he will continue contributing to basketball in other ways. Public opinion suggests that unsatisfactory national team performance is the main reason for his resignation.

title: Gold Price Plunges on November 7
content: On November 6, international precious metals prices fell sharply. Spot gold dropped nearly 3%, falling below $2,660 per ounce. Economists attributed the drop to uncertainty related to the U.S. presidential election. Chinese netizens reacted with comments like, 'Can it drop to 400? I want to buy gold bars!' and 'Let it drop a bit more, prices surged too much this year.'

title: Bee Flower's 'Fake Bestie' Ad Campaign Backfires
content: On November 7, Jiupai News reported that the official account of Bee Flower posted a controversial ad titled 'See What a Fake Bestie Looks Like,' which sparked criticism from netizens. Many found the content inappropriate. Bee Flower quickly issued an apology, stating that the post was deleted immediately and that a comprehensive internal review had begun. Public opinion emphasized that companies must remember to respect their audience and avoid offensive marketing tactics aimed purely at attracting attention.

title: Zhengzhou College Students Go Viral for Night Cycling to Kaifeng
content: Jimu News reported that college students in Zhengzhou recently went viral online for cycling at night to Kaifeng. They rented shared bikes in Jinshui District, rode more than 50 kilometers east along Zhengkai Avenue, and arrived in Kaifeng. After spending the night there, they returned to Zhengzhou by intercity train the next day. Netizens praised their youthful spirit but also raised safety concerns, urging for awareness of potential risks.

title: Zhuhai Police Report Major Vicious Case: 35 Dead, 43 Injured
content: On November 11, 2024, a man drove an off-road vehicle into citizens exercising inside Zhuhai Sports Center, resulting in 35 deaths and 43 injuries. The suspect, Fan (62, divorced), was subdued by police and hospitalized after attempting self-harm. The case was reportedly motivated by dissatisfaction over post-divorce property division. Fan is under criminal detention and an investigation is ongoing.

title: Spider-Man 4 Release Date Confirmed
content: Sony Pictures officially announced that the next Spider-Man movie starring Tom Holland is set for release in North American theaters on July 24, 2026. The announcement was made on October 28, 2024.

title: Holland Pulled Zendaya Out of the Crowd
content: Tom Holland pulled Zendaya away from invasive paparazzi in a crowd, gaining attention online.

title: Over 3,000 Children Killed in Gaza Within Three Weeks
content: Save the Children reported that within just three weeks, over 3,195 children were killed in Gaza since October 7, 2024, exceeding the annual average of child deaths in conflict zones worldwide since 2019. Additional deaths included 33 in the West Bank and 29 in Israel.

title: Trump Rally Speaker Launches Racist Tirade Against Latinos
content: At a Trump rally on October 27, comedian Tony Hinchcliffe made racist remarks targeting Puerto Ricans, Hispanics, Blacks, and Jews. He referred to Puerto Rico as a 'garbage island' and used offensive stereotypes. The event sparked outrage.

title: Tel Aviv Shooting: 6 Dead, 9 Injured
content: On October 1, two gunmen opened fire and stabbed people near a light rail station in Tel Aviv, killing 6 and injuring 9. Police identified the attackers as Palestinians from the West Bank and shot them on the spot.

title: Beyoncé Booed After Endorsing Kamala Harris Without Performing
content: At a Houston rally for Kamala Harris on October 25, Beyoncé gave a short 3-minute speech without performing, prompting boos from the audience. The event aimed to highlight abortion rights and voter mobilization, but the lack of performance disappointed many.

title: Elon Musk Attends Trump Rally, Declares Strong Support
content: On October 28, Elon Musk appeared with Donald Trump at a Pennsylvania rally, declaring Trump as the only option to preserve American democracy. Musk warned of dire consequences if Trump lost and used the 'Dark MAGA' motif to show support.

title: Trump Wins 2024 U.S. Presidential Election
content: In the early hours of November 6, Donald Trump declared victory in the 2024 U.S. election, becoming the first president since Grover Cleveland to serve non-consecutive terms. He won key swing states including North Carolina, Georgia, and Pennsylvania.

title: Giant Trump Parade Float Appears in Japan
content: On October 27, Trump supporters in Osaka, Japan paraded through the streets with a giant Trump float, waving U.S. and Japanese flags while playing Trump's 'Make America Great Again' slogan. The display drew widespread attention online.

title: UK Riots Reveal New Forms of Far-Right Organizing
content: After a stabbing incident in Liverpool on August 3, riots broke out in many towns in the UK. BBC analysis shows that far-right forces spread false information and incited riots online, but the violence was not planned by any single group.

title: League of Legends S14: T1 Defeats GEN to Reach Finals
content: On October 28, in the semi-finals of the League of Legends 2024 World Championship, T1 defeated GEN 3-1 to advance to the finals against BLG on November 2. MVPs included Gumayusi, Canyon, and Faker. Fans are eagerly anticipating the final showdown.

title: Macron Congratulates F. Lebrun on WTT Victory
content: On October 28, Felix Lebrun won the WTT Montpellier Championship, defeating Japan’s Tomokazu Harimoto 4-1 [11-7/11-9/11-6/8-11/11-4] in the men’s singles final. After the match, Lebrun shared a championship vlog on social media, where French President Emmanuel Macron commented, 'Congratulations, great champion!' At just 18 years old, Lebrun made history by winning France’s first WTT singles title, defeating strong opponents including Harimoto, Lin Shidong, Xiang Peng, Simon Gauzy, and even his brother Alexis Lebrun.

title: Trump Raises Right Fist After Being Shot at Rally
content: At 6:11 p.m. EDT on July 13, 2024, former U.S. President Donald Trump was shot at a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, by Thomas Matthew Crooks. Trump sustained an injury to his right ear, causing visible bleeding but was not seriously harmed. One rally attendee was killed and two others were seriously injured. Despite the injury, Trump stood up and raised his fist toward the crowd in a now-iconic image. He was stabilized at the hospital and flew to New Jersey that night. The next day, Trump was formally nominated as the Republican presidential candidate at the GOP National Convention in Milwaukee.

title: T1 Wins the League of Legends World Championship
content: On November 3, T1 claimed their fifth League of Legends World Championship title, marking their second consecutive global victory. The team, led by ZOFGK, thanked their loyal supporters with the message: 'To those who never gave up on us — this championship is for you!'

title: Macron Responds After Trump’s Victory: Europe Must Defend Its Interests
content: On November 7, following Trump's election victory, French President Emmanuel Macron stated: 'Americans have chosen Trump to defend American interests. As Europeans, we must ask ourselves: are we ready to defend European interests?' His remarks sparked discussions across Europe about the continent’s strategic autonomy.

title: Two Arrested After 4-Year-Old Attacked by Dogs in Xi’an
content: On January 21, in Huokou Village, Xi’an’s Baqiao District, a 4-year-old boy was mauled by two dogs while playing near the village entrance. The dogs were found to belong to a man named Guo, who failed to restrain them. After the attack, Guo attempted to evade responsibility by killing and burying the dogs elsewhere. Another individual, Zhang, helped him provide false information to the police. Both have now been criminally detained. Public opinion calls for strict dog ownership regulation and legal punishment for such negligence.

title: Ex-Coach Li Tie Sentenced to 20 Years
content: On January 13, the Xianning Intermediate Court sentenced Li Tie, former head coach of China's national football team, to 20 years in prison for bribery and corruption. The court ruled on multiple charges, including bribing and accepting bribes from public and private entities. The verdict was widely welcomed by Chinese football fans who have long demanded accountability.

title: Shanxi Reports Investigation Into Missing Female Master's Case
content: On January 10, Shanxi officials confirmed that criminal investigations have been launched in the case of a missing woman named Bu, who was later found. Authorities stated that several individuals have been criminally detained in relation to the case. Public opinion condemned efforts to whitewash a serious crime involving mental illness, sexual abuse, and forced childbirth.

title: Missing 19-Year-Old Student Found Dead in Chengdu
content: On January 13, Chengdu police confirmed the body of missing college student Jiang was recovered from the Tuo River. She had been missing since December 31, 2024. Her death was ruled a suicide after criticism over cheating. The case has sparked discussions on academic pressure and student mental health.

title: Jilin Company Replaces Wages with Consumer Vouchers
content: A company in Changchun, Jilin Province, issued consumer vouchers instead of cash wages, triggering public outrage. These vouchers were only usable in affiliated stores. Authorities have begun investigating the practice, which many believe violates labor laws.

title: Man Detained for Faking Subway Seat Sale Story
content: A man in Shanghai claimed on social media that he sold subway seats for 5 yuan during rush hour. The story was later found to be fabricated. He was administratively detained for spreading false information to gain online attention.

title: AI-Generated Earthquake Images Spark Disinformation Concerns
content: Following the 6.8 magnitude earthquake in Dingri County, Tibet, AI-generated images falsely depicting trapped children went viral. Authorities issued statements debunking the images and urged the public to rely on official sources and avoid spreading rumors.

title: Shanghai World Financial Center Fire Rumor Debunked
content: A viral video falsely claimed the Shanghai World Financial Center caught fire. Officials clarified that the white smoke seen was steam exhaust and not a fire. Similar rumors had appeared as early as 2017.

title: Hunan Student Missing After Traveling to Myanmar
content: A college student from Hunan was reported missing after traveling to Myanmar via Thailand. His sister stated that he had asked for academic leave and later disappeared. His last known location was traced to Myawaddy, Myanmar. Authorities are investigating.

title: TikTok Users Flock to Xiaohongshu Amid U.S. Ban Threat
content: Facing a potential U.S. ban, many TikTok users migrated to Chinese social app Xiaohongshu, which surged to the top of the App Store's U.S. free chart. Chinese netizens welcomed them warmly, saying, 'You're one of us now!'

title: Trump Announces U.S. Territorial Expansion Plans
content: Former President Donald Trump announced plans to expand U.S. territory during a recent campaign speech, sparking both national and international concern.

title: Actor Wang Xingtai Rescued from Trafficking at Myanmar Border
content: Chinese actor Wang Xingtai was confirmed to be a victim of human trafficking after being lured across the border into Myanmar. He has been rescued by Thai authorities. Other actors shared similar experiences of nearly being tricked into fake production teams. The case highlights the dangers of cross-border scams.
